decks.notes: This deck focuses on quickly ramping up mana using Mishra's Workshop and fast mana sources to play powerful artifacts like Karn, the Great Creator and The One Ring. It aims to overwhelm the opponent with aggressive creatures like Glaring Fleshraker and Patchwork Automaton while using cards like Manifold Key to control the board and generate card advantage. The goal is to establish a dominant board presence and quickly close out the game before the opponent has a chance to stabilize.

This deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan with hatebears like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex while also applying pressure with aggro creatures like Stillmoon Cavalier and White Plume Adventurer. It utilizes fast mana sources like Chrome Mox and the Moxen to accelerate into its threats early on. The inclusion of cards like Anointed Peacekeeper and March of Otherworldly Light help control the board and protect its creatures. The deck also includes disruptive lands like Wasteland and Karakas to further disrupt the opponent's strategy.

This deck aims to utilize powerful control elements such as counterspells, removal spells, and card advantage to dominate the game. It focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan while efficiently drawing cards and managing resources. The deck also features synergies with graveyard recursion and artifact mana acceleration to gain an advantage in the game. By controlling the pace of the game and making strategic decisions, the pilot of this deck can outmaneuver their opponent and come out on top in 1 vs 1 Vintage matches.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan with hatebears like Anointed Peacekeeper, Chancellor of the Annex, and Archon of Emeria, while also applying pressure with aggressive creatures like Seasoned Dungeoneer and Stillmoon Cavalier. It utilizes powerful artifacts like Chrome Mox and Moxen for fast mana acceleration, along with disruptive cards like Chalice of the Void and Wasteland. The deck aims to control the board and tempo of the game, punishing opponents for playing multiple spells per turn while developing its own board presence and beating down the opponent.

This Dimir Control deck focuses on utilizing cheap removal and countermagic spells to disrupt your opponent's game plan while generating card advantage through draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Treasure Cruise. The deck also includes powerful mana acceleration in the form of Black Lotus and Moxen, allowing you to cast your spells ahead of schedule. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value by allowing you to recur key creatures or artifacts from your graveyard. Overall, this deck aims to control the game and outvalue your opponent with efficient spells and card advantage.

The deck focuses on controlling the game by using a combination of counterspells, removal spells, and card draw. It utilizes powerful cards like Force of Will, Swords to Plowshares, and Ancestral Recall to disrupt the opponent's game plan while maintaining card advantage with cards like Treasure Cruise and Dig Through Time. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value through recursion of cheap permanents. The deck aims to outlast the opponent by effectively managing threats and resources to secure victory through attrition.

This deck focuses on deploying powerful artifact creatures and disrupting the opponent's game plan with taxing effects. It utilizes cards like Mishra's Workshop and Ancient Tomb to quickly ramp out threats like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Stonecoil Serpent. It also includes cards like Sphere of Resistance and Trinisphere to slow down the opponent's spells, while Null Rod and Lodestone Golem shut down artifact strategies. The deck can easily lock opponents out of the game with its disruptive elements and overwhelming board presence, making it a formidable Aggro - MUD archetype in Vintage 1 vs 1.

This deck focuses on using the powerful artifact Paradoxical Outcome to generate a large amount of card advantage and mana acceleration. By combining artifact mana sources like Black Lotus and Moxen with Tolarian Academy, the deck can quickly generate a large amount of mana to cast game-winning spells like Time Walk and Ancestral Recall. The deck also utilizes counterspells like Force of Will and interaction like Swords to Plowshares to protect its combo pieces and disrupt the opponent's game plan. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds another layer of flexibility and resilience to the deck.

This deck aims to quickly assemble the Time Vault + Voltaic Key combo to take infinite turns, utilizing powerful acceleration from cards like Mishra's Workshop and Grim Monolith. The deck also utilizes Coveted Jewel to generate card advantage and disrupt opponents. Force of Will helps protect key combo pieces, while Paradoxical Outcome provides card draw and potential for explosive turns. Various mana rocks and land cards help to ensure the deck can consistently hit its powerful combo pieces, allowing for quick and decisive victories.

The deck focuses on using efficient creatures and disruptive spells to control the board and pressure the opponent. By combining aggressive creatures like Dreadhorde Arcanist and Thundertrap Trainer with powerful utility spells like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares, it aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while attacking their life total. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value and recursion, making the deck resilient and difficult to deal with. Overall, it aims to quickly establish dominance and stay ahead of the opponent with its proactive playstyle.

The deck focuses on disrupting opponents with hatebear creatures while applying pressure with aggressive creatures. It also utilizes resource denial through cards like Strip Mine and Wasteland, and accelerates mana with powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and the Moxen. The deck aims to control the tempo of the game by slowing down opponents' strategies and overwhelming them with a combination of disruptive creatures and efficient beaters.

The deck focuses on quickly deploying Atraxa, Grand Unifier using Oath of Druids and Show and Tell, while controlling the game with counterspells like Force of Will and disruptive cards like Narset, Parter of Veils. It also includes card advantage engines like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time to maintain a strong hand. The inclusion of Oko, Thief of Crowns provides additional disruption and removal options. Overall, the deck aims to quickly assemble a powerful board presence while disrupting the opponent's game plan.

The main focus of this Dimir Control deck is to disrupt your opponent's plans while maintaining card advantage and control over the game. By utilizing powerful disruption spells like Force of Will and Fatal Push, along with card draw options like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time, the deck aims to control the game's tempo and prevent the opponent from gaining an advantage. Additionally, the inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds an extra layer of recursion and value to keep the game in your favor.

The main concept of this deck is to aggressively use cards like Bazaar of Baghdad, Hollow One, and Vengevine to quickly overwhelm the opponent. By utilizing a mix of efficient creatures, disruptive counterspells, and graveyard recursion, the deck aims to put pressure on the opponent while disrupting their game plan. With a focus on generating early game advantage and maintaining board presence, the deck seeks to win the game before the opponent has a chance to stabilize. The inclusion of Force of Will and other counter spells helps protect the deck's game plan and prevent the opponent from mounting a successful defense.

This deck focuses on using Oath of Druids to cheat powerful creatures into play, while also maintaining control over the opponent's plays using counterspells, removal, and disruptive cards like Null Rod. The key strategy is to ramp into Oath of Druids as quickly as possible, protecting it with counterspells, and then using it to get Atraxa or other powerful creatures onto the battlefield, overwhelming the opponent with strong threats. Additionally, the deck includes versatile cards like Dack Fayden and Dig Through Time to provide card advantage and flexibility in different situations.

The deck focuses on generating mana quickly with Mishra's Workshop, Ancient Tomb, and Grim Monolith to cast powerful artifacts like The One Ring and Coveted Jewel. It utilizes cards like Paradoxical Outcome and Tolarian Academy to draw cards and search for combo pieces like Time Vault and Trinisphere. The deck also includes disruptive cards like Force of Will and Sink into Stupor to control the game. By assembling key artifacts and controlling the board, the deck aims to outvalue and outmaneuver opponents in a fast-paced Vintage 1 vs 1 format.
